[Interview, 2004-06-19, CNN LARRY KING LIVE]
HOST: Did you ever have a doubt in this case that you had the wrong man?

HOST: In other words, you...

HOST: You don't want to see people have evidence against them. You want -- you want it so you can clear them, right?

HOST: Yes.

HOST: Yes.

HOST: And Phil, do you think about it?

HOST: Was it a slam dunk?

HOST: All right. Let's discuss some of the things said in interviews about some of you. About Denise O.J. said recently, "I am sure the income is down on the foundation that she works for, which I would imagine makes her income go down. I don't think anyone's bills have been paid more than Denise's from what came from this trial." The contention is you have profited from this death.

HOST: She wanted...

HOST: ...bad things about your sister?

HOST: Why does O.J. pick on you, do you think?

HOST: You were so vehement...

HOST: You were so vehement about him, right?

HOST: We're back. About GUEST, O.J. has said that you took advantage of this, and people like you and Marcia Clark got such an opportunity from this. People signed them to contracts -- accusing you of profiting off of your son's death.
GUEST: The man is a damn liar, OK? We haven't signed contract one and haven't profited in any way or benefited in any way. To even suggest that gives you an indication of what kind of a sick SOB this guy is.

HOST: Why did you...
GUEST: How dare he suggest that any of us profited in any way? We have all lost the most precious thing on the face of the earth, and this guy thinks in terms of how people profit. The only one that gained from this was him. He retains his life, his freedom and his chance to continue day after day. He's the one that profited.

HOST: Why did you collect no money?
GUEST: Well, first of all, he makes a point of telling the world on a regular basis that he will never pay a dime of that judgment, that he'll do whatever he has to do not to pay a dime. So that's No. 1. No. 2, he has moved to Florida to make sure that he protects whatever he has additionally. He protects some income that he makes, and he protects his home. So he's never going to pay a dime...

HOST: Florida is, like, a debtors' state, right?
GUEST: Right. He's going to make certain, no matter what he does, that he never honors the judgment, that which the vast majority of people in this country would have to do if they had a judgment against them.

HOST: Kim, what do you make of him?

HOST: I know.

HOST: Were you at his arrest, Tom?

HOST: Yes.

HOST: You were there, Phil?

HOST: Yes.

HOST: Why?

HOST: It was so early.

HOST: What do you mean by a prosecutor on the defense?

HOST: You mean she was on the defensive?

HOST: What was it like? You believe he killed your sister.

HOST: You believe he killed your son?
GUEST: Without a question.

HOST: To sit in the same room with him at a deposition.

HOST: Did he look at you?
GUEST: Yes, and always with a snotty little glare. He was an arrogant -- I can't use the words on TV.

HOST: By your side or...
GUEST: By our side. And he was doing the following, "Hmm- hmm, mm-mm, mm-mm," or he'd lean way back in his chair with his eyes closed, and that's how he was -- that's how serious he took this whole thing. He couldn't have cared less. He was at complete peace.

HOST: GUEST, what are you doing?
GUEST: I'm working.

HOST: When did you think it was O.J.?
GUEST: Absolutely for sure at the time the DNA evidence started hitting. We were -- we talked as a family and were willing to keep an open mind.

HOST: Gave him the benefit.
GUEST: Gave him the benefit. But the more evidence that came in, the more it became more and more obvious, and, once that DNA evidence hit, it was slam dunk for us.

HOST: Did you know it right away, Tom?

HOST: Phil?

HOST: Why does it seemingly not go away, do you think?

HOST: ...of Scott Peterson, it's the forerunner of all murder trials.

HOST: Did you watch any of his appearances? Would you watch him?

HOST: Yeah, but you wouldn't watch?

[Interview, 2006-09-05, NANCY GRACE]
HOST: OK.

HOST: And?

HOST: So what?

HOST: With us tonight, in defense of John Mark Karr, the Karr family attorney, Gary Harris. A very well-respected lawyer in his jurisdiction. Mr. Harris, speaking of him being loyal, as he described it, how long has it been since he`s seen his children?

HOST: Why?

HOST: Correct.

HOST: I believe you said 2001. That`s been five years.

HOST: Has he contacted them? E-mail, letter, gift, photo, nothing?

HOST: Then why are they defending him now and saying that there is no way -- and you -- saying there is no way he`s a threat to children?

[Interview, 2006-11-19, CNN LARRY KING LIVE]
HOST: Kim, how did you react?

HOST: But they are all...

HOST: You know, GUEST, these days the talk is always of closure. Could it be -- could there be one good side of this that in admitting this you're at least finding out what actually happened that night?
GUEST: You know what, first of all I don't imagine for one second that he considers this admitting it but put that aside. No, there's not going to be ever any closure to this. I know what he did. Kim knows what he did. The vast majority of right thinking Americans or people around the world know what he did. He butchered two people and walked out of a courtroom a free man. And now he is glorifying it in a book. And, as Kim said a minute ago, he is willing, as sick a guy as he is, he is willing to put in a book and on air, he's willing to tell the world how he "would" murder his children's mother and Ron, sick.

HOST: Why do you think, I mean you're not stupid, why do you think he's doing this, Kim?

HOST: Even though it's negative?

HOST: Do you think it's going to sell?

HOST: A little weird.
